_readme: Whole calls, driven end to end against a real provider.
Every live test but guard detection is here. These run a call from the
greeting to the closing line — every question, every model call, the real
planner deciding what comes next — and check what came out the other end.
That is the only place several things can be seen at all: that question 1a is
asked and 1b is not, that question 5 appears for a high-risk member and is
reported as skipped for a rising one, that a correction re-opens a branch, and
that the disposition matches what actually happened on the call.
The member is scripted, not generated. Their replies are keyed by the slot the
agent is waiting on, so the script answers whatever it is actually asked
rather than assuming an order — if the planner asks something unexpected, the
call runs out of replies and the test says which question had none.
Fields:
payload      the work item, as the platform would send it
replies      slot -> what the member says when asked for it
expect.disposition   how the call must end
expect.answers       slot -> the value that must be in the outcome
expect.not_asked     slots the member must never be asked for
expect.skipped       slots the outcome must report as skipped
expect.not_declined  slots the outcome must NOT report as declined
expect.declined      slots the outcome MUST report as declined
expect.reported_intents      kinds that MUST reach the outcome's open_intents
expect.not_reported_intents  kinds that must NOT be in it
A guard mid-call needs no special mechanism: make the guard line the reply to
whichever question it should interrupt.
A call is expensive — roughly ten agent turns and up to three model calls
each — so a scenario is worth adding when it shows something a shorter one
cannot, and worth loading up when it can: several of these carry four or five
unrelated rules on different questions of the same survey, because the member
is answering nine questions either way.
One rule about the replies: keep the GATES unambiguous. Identity and consent
are not what these calls are testing, and a gate that fails ends the call
before the interesting part, reporting ended_early and hiding whatever the
scenario was actually for. Save the idiom, the hesitation and the oblique
phrasing for the survey questions and the guard interjections, where a
misread is the finding rather than a wall in front of one.

why: A member who did not catch the question, twice, and answered both times once
they had. Nothing here is a refusal and nothing here is an unclear answer, so
the call must end 'surveyed' with both ratings in the file.
This is the end-to-end half of the repeat-request work: the single-turn
scenarios check the label, and only a whole call can show what the label COSTS.
Read as unclear answers these turns spend the slot's retry budget, and the
outcome reports a member who was trying to answer as one who would rather not
say. The second one is a repeat asked mid-answer, which must not leave half a
rating behind either.

reviewed_resources: What counts as a resource, exactly?
Does that include the calls with my coach?
Right — then yes, I looked at a few of the articles.

why: Two questions back before the member could answer the first question, and the
second is one the script has no answer to. Both must be treated as somebody
working out what is being asked, not as somebody failing to answer it.
The 'yes' at the end is the one that matters: a clarifying question must never
be guessed into an answer, and the answer that eventually comes must still land.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes I did, and they were somewhat helpful actually — I've started walking every morning because of them.
replies.improvement_feedback: No, nothing I can think of.

replies.staff_helpful: Yes, they were good with me.

why: One call carrying four things that are each not what they look like, because
each one used to be reported as a member who would not answer:
- answering 1a and 1b in one breath. Both must land, and 1b must not be put
again to somebody who has already answered it.
- 'no, nothing I can think of' on a feedback question IS the answer.
- 'I couldn't tell you' is not knowing, not refusing. It is re-asked.
- 'it was alright, can't complain' is not a rating. The nearest option is
somewhat_helpful and recording it would put a rating in this member's file
that she never gave — so the turn records NOTHING and the rating that
arrives second is the one reported.
The restraint is the load-bearing half and the hard half: there is always a
nearest option. What proves it end to end is that overall_experience comes out
extremely_helpful — the answer she gave — and not somewhat_helpful, the answer
she was nearest to.
resource_helpfulness carries a reply she should never need to give. If it is
put to her at all, the call still finishes — and fails saying she was asked
something she had already answered, which is the finding, rather than dying on
a missing script line.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look at some of them.

replies.no_review_reason: I never had the time, if I'm honest.

why: A member correcting an answer four questions after she gave it, which no other
whole call does.
Three things have to happen at once and only a whole call shows them together:
the revision arrives as a correction rather than as a fresh value, question 1b
opens because the answer that closed it has changed, and the helpfulness rating
she already gave is dropped rather than left behind on a question this member
is no longer being asked. A rating for resources she never opened is worse than
no rating, and it is invisible in the answers unless something checks that it
went.
It must also not cost her the question she was actually asked: correcting an
earlier answer is a contribution, not a failure to answer improvement_feedback.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of the articles. Sorry — my daughter's just arrived, she visits on Thursdays.
replies.resource_helpfulness: Somewhat helpful. While I've got you, when is somebody getting back to me about the physio bill? Nobody's rung.
replies.improvement_feedback: Nothing really. Could you email me a copy of what I've said today?

why: Three unrelated things raised in one survey, and the call owes each of them
something different. Every one of them used to be filed identically, as a side
request, and reported at the end as an outstanding member request.
- her daughter arriving asks nothing of us. It is heard and it is not work.
- the physio bill is the one with consequences: somebody is waiting. Note that
none of the ten member-services keywords appears in it — the classification
is the model's, and this is the turn that used to fall through the list.
- the copy of her answers is the genuinely actionable one, and the only thing
here that nobody on this call can do.
What is asserted is the report a person actually works through: the bill and the
request in it, the chit-chat not. A call that reports all three is a call whose
list nobody reads, which is how the bill gets missed.
The answers must survive all of it. A member who talks while she answers has
still answered.

replies.reached_policyholder: She's my mother — she's having a nap just now. Can I take a message?

why: The other half of wrong_number_ends_the_call, and the distinction between them
is a work item worth retrying tomorrow versus a number that must never be
dialled for this member again.
Nobody said the word 'no'. Telling us the policyholder cannot come to the phone
IS the answer to whether we reached her, and the survey must not be put to the
daughter who answered — she never consented to anything and the answers would
not be her mother's.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of them.
resource_helpfulness: I'm not sure I follow you — helpful how, exactly?
Oh, I see what you mean. Somewhat helpful, then.

why: Confusion is not an unclear answer. 'Helpful how, exactly?' is somebody who
has not been asked the question in terms she can answer yet, and reading it as
a failed attempt charges her for it — three of those and the question is filed
as one she would rather not answer.
Two things are asserted and the second is the newer one: the rating she gives
once she understands must land, AND her question must not still be sitting in
the report at the end of the call. Putting the question again IS the answer to
it, so nothing is owed by the time the call closes.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I looked at some.
replies.resource_helpfulness: Oh, it's hard to say really. They were what they were.

why: Retry exhaustion, which every other call avoids. She says the same unusable
thing however often it is put, and 'they were what they were' is not one of the
four options at any point.
Three things have to be true at once. Nothing is recorded — the nearest option
is somewhat_helpful and it is still a guess. The question stops being asked
rather than going round for ever. And on the third failed attempt the call
hands off to a representative.
This is the one place 'declined' is asserted as something that MUST happen.
Everywhere else it is the thing that must not.

replies.reviewed_resources: Actually, could I speak to a real person about all this?

why: The escalation nobody is in danger from, and the one this suite never covered
end to end — safeguarding was tested as a whole call and this was not.
A member who asks for a person gets a person: the survey stops where it is, the
approved handoff line is said exactly as written, and the call is handed over
with a reason a human can read. Carrying on to question 1b after somebody has
asked to speak to someone is the rudest thing this agent could do.

replies.reached_policyholder: Hello, you've reached Margaret. I'm not able to take your call right now — please leave a message after the tone.
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: A recording cannot consent to anything. The voicemail message is left and the
call ends there — a survey put to an answering machine would produce answers
attributed to a member who never picked up the phone.
The guard file tests whether this turn is RECOGNISED. Only a whole call shows
what happens next, which is the part that matters: the approved voicemail
wording, said exactly, and nothing asked after it.

reviewed_resources: Hang on love, there's somebody at the door.
Sorry — one moment, the kettle's going.
Just a second, let me find my glasses.
Hold on, the dog's at it again.

why: The other end of hold_then_carries_on. A member who keeps stepping away is not
refusing anything, and the agent waits — but not for ever, and not by talking
into an empty room.
max_consecutive_holds is 3, so the fourth ends the call with a representative
handoff — somebody who never came back to the phone needs a person to follow up,
not a polite goodbye to an empty room.

replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: A gate that never settles. There is no version of this survey that runs without
knowing who is on the line, so once max_identity_asks is spent the call hands
off to a representative rather than ending blindly — a member who will not say
who they are needs a person, not a polite goodbye.
max_identity_asks is 2, and asking us who WE are does not spend a retry but
does spend an ask, so a member who says 'who's asking?' twice has this call
handed off on her third turn.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of the articles.
replies.liked_most: I'd rather not get into all that, if it's all the same to you.

why: A real refusal, which is different from all four of the things that merely look
like one. She would rather not say, on one question, and that is an answer
about the survey rather than a failure of the call: it is recorded, the call
goes on, and nothing is escalated over it.
The pairing is the point. 'Nothing really' on improvement_feedback is an answer
and must NOT be declined; 'I'd rather not get into all that' on the very next
question must be. They are one sentence apart in the transcript and a survey
apart in the result.

replies.participation_consent: Not just now, I'm in the middle of something.

Really, I have no preference — any time is fine.
I genuinely don't mind, just call whenever.
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: A reschedule where the member never names a time, on a rising-tier member so
the tier is not always the high one in the interesting calls.
The agent asks up to max_asks_per_slot times for a specific date or time.
Vague answers ('whenever suits you', 'any time is fine') do not satisfy the
check and trigger a retry with a nudge. On the final attempt the agent accepts
whatever the member says and closes as reschedule_requested — the callback team
will handle scheduling. The call must never slide into the survey questions
because consent was never given.

replies.reached_policyholder: The person you are trying to reach is not available. Please record your message after the tone.
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: A carrier network announcement rather than the member's own personal greeting.
The wording matches the voicemail.carrier_announcement guard scenario, which
tests whether the pattern is RECOGNISED in isolation — this is the end-to-end
half: what the call does once it recognises one.
The approved voicemail message must be spoken verbatim and the call must end
there. A carrier announcement cannot consent to anything and must never be
surveyed.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of the articles.
improvement_feedback: I think we should have more chickens. Chickens are very helpful for everyone.
More regular phone check-ins would be nice.
replies.liked_most: The articles were clear and easy to read.

why: A completely off-topic response on a feedback question must redirect the member
back to the survey rather than accepting it or treating it as a refusal.
The first reply to improvement_feedback mentions chickens — entirely unrelated to
an aging-in-place program — and must not be recorded. The agent asks again. The
second reply is genuine feedback and must land. The call ends surveyed and the
slot must not appear as declined — the member answered once redirected.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I looked at a few.
replies.liked_most: The articles were easy to follow.
overall_experience: I would say it's somewhere between extremely helpful and somewhat helpful.

why: An ambiguous answer on a choice question must be retried — with different wording
rather than a verbatim repeat — and the answer that arrives on the second attempt
must land.
The first reply to overall_experience is 'somewhere between extremely helpful and
somewhat helpful', which cannot be mapped to any single option. The agent asks
again. The second reply is unambiguous and must be recorded as somewhat_helpful.
Two things are asserted: the correct answer lands, and the slot is not reported
as declined — a member who needed one re-ask is not a member who refused.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of the articles.
liked_most: My cat is called Biscuit and she sits on my lap every morning.
I had minestrone soup for lunch. Very warming.
The neighbours have a new car. Red, it is.

why: Off-topic answers on a feedback question spend the retry budget just as unclear
answers do. When the budget runs out the question is reported as declined and the
call hands off to a representative.
All three replies to liked_most are entirely unrelated to the program — a cat,
soup, and a neighbour's car. Each one triggers a redirect. On the third the
budget is exhausted, the slot is declined, and the call escalates.
This is the pairing for off_topic_feedback_redirected_and_answered: one shows
that off-topic handling redirects without charging a decline when the member
eventually answers; this one shows it eventually does charge, and that
budget exhaustion hands the call to a representative.

replies.reached_policyholder: Please take this number off your list — I've already asked twice to be removed and I don't want any more calls.
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: A DNC request at the very first member turn — before identity is confirmed and
before consent is asked. Every other DNC test fires mid-survey.
The guard must catch it at the opening line, end the call immediately, and
never ask anything after it. No survey question may reach a member who has
explicitly asked not to be called.

replies.reviewed_resources: Oh yes, I read all of them — extremely helpful they were. And I'd recommend the program to anyone, without a doubt.
replies.liked_most: The information packs were very clear.

why: A member who gives three answers in one breath: Q1a, Q1b, and Q4. The whole
questionnaire is offered to the extractor every turn so an answer volunteered
ahead of its question is just as valid as one given when it is put.
resource_helpfulness and would_recommend must not be asked again. The slots are
already answered, and putting them a second time would be asking a member who
was being helpful to repeat herself.
This is the most forward version of the multi-answer case: three slots from one
turn, skipping all the questions in between.

replies.reached_policyholder: Yes, I'm Margaret. I'll be honest with you — I've been feeling very low lately. Some mornings I wonder what the point of getting up is.
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: Safeguarding at the very first member turn — before consent, before any survey
question. Every other safeguarding whole-call test fires mid-survey.
The guard runs on every turn, including the identity turn, and a member at risk
must be handed to a person immediately regardless of where in the call they say
it. Asking consent of someone who has just disclosed distress would be wrong,
and the survey must not start.

reached_policyholder: Sorry, who are you with — is this something I signed up for?
Ah right, yes — that's me, Margaret. Go on then.
replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of the articles.

why: The identity success path that will_not_say_who_she_is never reaches. A member
who asks who is calling before confirming spends an identity ask — the agent
explains itself and puts the question again — but confirms on the second attempt
and the survey continues normally.
This is the pairing for will_not_say_who_she_is: that one shows the failure path
(representative handoff after max_identity_asks); this one shows that the same
opening does not have to end that way. An ask does not become a refusal until
the budget is gone.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read a few of them.
replies.improvement_feedback: Actually — I was too modest a moment ago. The resources were extremely helpful, not just somewhat. As for improvements, more regular phone calls would be nice.
replies.liked_most: The articles were easy to understand.

why: A correction that updates a choice rating without reopening any branch.
a_correction_reopens_the_other_branch tests a correction that changes the
survey's structure — reviewed_resources flipping from yes to no closes one
branch and opens another. This one is the simpler case: the member revises
resource_helpfulness from somewhat_helpful to extremely_helpful while answering
the next question. The branch stays the same (reviewed_resources is still yes,
no_review_reason is never asked), and only the rating changes.
Two things must be true: the corrected rating is what reaches the outcome, not
the original one; and the correction must not charge a retry against the slot
it arrived alongside — improvement_feedback must not appear as declined.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of them.
replies.resource_helpfulness: Somewhat helpful, I suppose — though I have to say, none of it really matters. I've been feeling so low lately I can't see the point in anything any more.

why: A safeguarding disclosure embedded in the same turn as a survey answer.
safeguarding_stops_the_survey_mid_call keeps the two on separate turns: the
rating lands cleanly, then the disclosure arrives on the next question and the
call hands off. Here they arrive together. The guard and the extractor run
concurrently; when the guard fires, the extractor's output is discarded — so
resource_helpfulness must NOT appear in the outcome, even though the member
said 'somewhat helpful' in the same breath.
The question is whether the call protects the member correctly when the urgent
signal arrives alongside ordinary content. reviewed_resources from the previous
turn is kept — only this turn's reading is thrown away — and nothing is asked
after the handoff.

reviewed_resources: Just give me a minute, I need to sit down.
Sorry — I've gone blank. What was the question again?
Yes, I did read through several of them.
replies.liked_most: The information was easy to follow.

why: Three replies on one slot: a pause, a confused return, then the real answer.
hold_then_carries_on is one clean pause followed by a clean answer. This one
is the messier version from a real call: the member steps away, comes back
without knowing what was being asked, and has to be told again before she can
answer. Neither the pause nor the blank return charges a retry — the member
has not failed to answer, she has simply not been in a position to yet.
Three things must hold: the slot is answered once she is back, the retry budget
is not spent on turns that were not refusals, and the slot must not appear in
declined.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yeah. You know what? My daughter was round at the weekend — she's always on at me about my health — but yes, I did look through a few of the articles.
replies.liked_most: The nurse was very patient with me.

why: A yes buried inside a conversational ramble. The member answers the question
correctly but surrounds it with off-topic content about her daughter.
Every other yes/no test has a clean, direct answer. Real calls do not. A member
who says 'yeah... but yes, I did read them' has answered yes — the surrounding
noise must not prevent it from landing, and the off-topic content must not be
mistaken for a refusal or for survey content.
This mirrors the pattern seen in live calls where a brief affirmative arrives
alongside an unrelated remark.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read a few.
resource_helpfulness: Somewhere between extremely helpful and somewhat helpful.
I'd say somewhere in the middle — between somewhat helpful and not very helpful.
It's really hard to pick one. Somewhere between the options, if I'm honest.

why: The 'somewhere between' exhaustion pattern, drawn from real calls. The member
genuinely cannot commit to a single option and says so three times — the
wording changes but never resolves to one of the four choices.
one_question_never_gets_a_usable_answer covers exhaustion with vague non-answers
('they were what they were'). This is the structurally identical but linguistically
distinct case: the member IS engaging with the options and naming them, but
she is placing herself between them rather than on one. Neither 'between
extremely helpful and somewhat helpful' nor 'somewhere in the middle' maps to
any single option — recording the nearest would be a guess.
Three things must hold: nothing is recorded (no guess), the question stops
being asked, and the call hands off to a representative.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes.

why: Single-word and two-word answers throughout. The whole survey, minimal input.
Every other test uses natural-length replies. Real calls also contain members
who say as little as possible — 'yes', 'yeah', 'none', 'no' — and each of
those must still land. A pipeline that works on 'Yes, I read several of the
articles and found them helpful' must also work on 'Yes.'
The negative-leaning answers are deliberate: this member is not enthusiastic
and her terseness reflects it. 'No.' for would_recommend and 'Not very helpful'
for overall_experience are still valid answers, and a short reply is not a
refusal.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of them.
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular check-ins would be nice.
would_recommend: Why do they always ask you this sort of thing? I don't know what difference it makes.
Yes, I would. The nurse was excellent.

why: A member who grumbles about being asked a question before she answers it.
The first reply to would_recommend is frustration about the survey itself — not
an answer to whether she would recommend the program, and not a refusal either.
The agent must not record it as a no (she did not say no), must not treat it as
a refusal (she did not decline), and must ask the question again.
The second reply is the real answer and must land. The slot must not appear in
declined — a member who needed the question put twice because she was venting
first has still answered it.

reviewed_resources: Before we go any further — I've been having trouble with a credit card charge. Can you help me dispute it?
Yes, I did look through a few of the articles.
replies.liked_most: The articles were very clearly written.

why: A standalone out-of-scope service request — a credit card dispute — given instead
of answering the first survey question. The agent must say it cannot help with
that on this call and re-ask, without charging the retry budget against the member.
The intent stays in the outcome so a person can follow up. reviewed_resources must
not appear as declined — the member answered it once redirected.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look.
resource_helpfulness: Can I ask you something first — my insurance premium went up last month and nobody has explained why. Can you look into that?
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular phone calls would be nice.
replies.liked_most: The nurse I spoke to was excellent.

why: A standalone insurance query raised in place of a survey answer, mid-survey on a
rising-tier member. The agent must acknowledge it cannot help with insurance on
this call and re-ask without spending a retry.
Rising-tier variant: confirms staff_helpful is never asked while also covering
the freeform acknowledgement behaviour on a different question and member tier.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read a few — though while I have you, I'd like to dispute a credit card charge. Can anyone help with that?
replies.liked_most: The information was easy to understand.

why: The member answers the survey question AND raises an out-of-scope service request
in the same breath. The answer must land, the survey must move on, and the credit
card request must be acknowledged as something this call cannot act on and reported.
No retry is triggered — the member answered. Paired with standalone_credit_card_
blocks_then_answers which covers the version where no answer came with the request.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look at a few of them.
replies.resource_helpfulness: Somewhat helpful. I also want to ask — I received an invoice I don't understand. Is there someone I can speak to about that?
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular check-ins would be nice.

why: Answer plus billing query in one turn at the helpfulness question. The rating must
be recorded and the survey must continue — the billing enquiry cannot be actioned
but must be acknowledged and reported for a person to follow up.
The correct wording is 'I'm not able to help with that on this call' — not 'I'll
note that and pass it on to the program team', which implies the program team
handles invoice queries.

reviewed_resources: Sorry — what is this survey actually about? I'm not entirely sure what I signed up for.
Ah right, yes — I did go through some of the articles.

why: The member asks what the survey is about before answering the first question.
The agent must answer — explain it is a short satisfaction survey about their
experience with the Sagility Smart Step program — and then re-ask.
The member's question must be answered, not ignored or treated as a failed
attempt. Once the survey question is re-asked and answered, the clarification is
resolved and must not remain in the outcome.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read some of the articles.
resource_helpfulness: What exactly is the difference between extremely helpful and somewhat helpful?
replies.liked_most: The information packs were very clear.

why: The member asks what two of the rating options mean before she can answer. The
agent must explain the distinction briefly and re-ask the question with all options.
Distinct from general confusion ('I'm not sure I follow'): she is asking a precise
question about specific options. She has not failed to answer — she has not yet
been given enough information to answer. Once re-asked, her rating must land and
the clarification must be resolved, not left in the outcome.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of them.
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular phone calls would be nice — though can I ask, what do you actually do with these answers?

why: The member gives improvement feedback and asks what the survey results are used for
— an answerable question about the call itself. The agent must address it briefly
and move on to the next question.
The feedback answer must land. The clarification is resolved once addressed:
asking what happens to the answers is within the survey context and once spoken to
there is nothing left to report.

replies.participation_consent: Yes, but could you tell me what sort of questions you'll be asking?
replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read through a few.
replies.liked_most: The information was very easy to follow.

why: The member grants consent AND asks what the survey questions will cover in one
turn. Consent must be recorded as granted and the survey must proceed. The agent
must answer the scope question before leading into the first question — not ignore it.
The clarification is resolved when consent is recorded and the survey begins.
Asking what will be covered is a question about this call, answered by the act of
starting the survey, and must not remain in the outcome.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, a few of the articles.
replies.improvement_feedback: Nothing really — I had a lovely bowl of tomato soup at lunch, completely off the subject!

why: The member gives a valid feedback answer ('nothing really') and appends an
off-topic aside about food. The answer must land. The aside must not prevent the
call from moving forward, must not be mistaken for survey content, and must not
appear in the outcome — food comments ask nothing of a person.
With requires_free_flow set for aside intents, the agent briefly acknowledges
('That's not something I can help with') before continuing, rather than silently
ignoring it or treating the whole turn as off-topic.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read through a few — I was also hoping to ask about my benefits, but I suppose that's not what this is about?
replies.improvement_feedback: More check-ins would help. And while I've got someone on the line — there is a claim from two months ago I've heard nothing about.

why: Out-of-scope service requests at two separate questions — a benefits query at
question 1 and an unresolved claim at the improvement feedback question. Both
arrive alongside an answer so neither triggers a retry.
Asserts the unsupported kind appears in the outcome: a person needs to see both
entries, and this is the survey-level check that neither is silently dropped. The
answers must also land, confirming the survey progressed normally around both.

replies.reviewed_resources: Oh, yes. The videos mostly.
replies.liked_most: The videos were easy to follow.

why: The exact live-call pattern that triggered the AMBIGUOUS misclassification fix:
'Oh, yes. The videos mostly.' is a yes/no answer followed by elaboration.
The elaboration ('the videos mostly') is context, not ambiguity. A yes that
arrives with a reason or qualifier is still a yes. reviewed_resources must land
as 'yes' on the first attempt with no retry and no declined flag.

replies.reviewed_resources: No, I never got round to them. Been very busy at home lately.
replies.no_review_reason: No time, really — just too much on.
replies.improvement_feedback: Maybe more reminders to look at the resources.
replies.liked_most: The nurse I spoke to was very kind.

why: A no answer with an appended reason at reviewed_resources. The reason does not
make the answer ambiguous — 'No, I never got round to them. Been very busy'
is a clear no followed by context.
reviewed_resources must land as 'no' without retry, taking the no_review_reason
branch. resource_helpfulness must never be asked. Paired with
yes_with_elaboration_at_reviewed_resources: both directions of the branch must
survive elaboration.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look.

why: A trailing fragment ('They were—') at the helpfulness question followed by
a clear answer on the re-ask.
The first reply breaks off mid-phrase and must be classified as AMBIGUOUS —
nothing can be inferred from an incomplete sentence. The agent re-asks.
On the second attempt 'Extremely helpful' maps cleanly to one option and must
be recorded. resource_helpfulness must not appear as declined — one incomplete
reply does not exhaust the retry budget.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read a few.

why: Trailing fragment at the final choice question — the last question asked before
the survey closes. 'I would say it was—' is an incomplete sentence and must not
be completed by inference.
The agent must re-ask overall_experience. On the second reply 'Somewhat helpful'
maps to one option and must be recorded. The slot must not appear as declined.
Rising-tier member confirms staff_helpful is never asked.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of the articles.
replies.would_recommend: Yes, absolutely. I've already mentioned it to my sister.

why: Yes with immediate reinforcement and a personal anecdote at would_recommend.
'Yes, absolutely. I've already mentioned it to my sister.' is a clear yes with
context that must not trigger a retry or count as ambiguous.
The anecdote about mentioning it to her sister is not a survey answer for any
other slot and must not be mistaken for one.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read some.
replies.improvement_feedback: More support in the early weeks would help.
replies.would_recommend: No, not really. I don't know many people who'd be in that situation, to be honest.

why: A no with an appended explanation at would_recommend. 'No, not really. I don't
know many people who'd be in that situation' is a clear no — the reason that
follows does not make it ambiguous or a refusal.
Paired with yes_with_elaboration_at_would_recommend: both directions must
survive elaboration on this question. The negative-leaning answers throughout
confirm the pipeline handles an unenthusiastic-but-complete survey correctly.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I read several.
replies.liked_most: The walking plan was very practical.
replies.staff_helpful: Oh yes, very much so. They were always patient and clear with me.

why: 'Oh yes, very much so. They were always patient and clear with me.' is a yes
reinforced with praise. The praise is context, not a second survey answer.
staff_helpful is the only yes/no question exclusive to high-risk members. This
is its dedicated ambiguous-elaboration test, confirming the fix applies to the
gate-guarded question as well as the open ones.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I looked at some.
replies.liked_most: The information was easy to understand.

why: Trailing fragment ('I suppose I—') at would_recommend then a clear answer on
the re-ask. Covers the second yes/no survey question beyond reviewed_resources.
Rising-tier member so the call is shorter and the fragment is the only
complexity — isolating the trailing-fragment behaviour on this slot without
any other unusual turn.

replies.participation_consent: Yes, I've got a few minutes — go ahead.
replies.reviewed_resources: Oh, yes. A few of the articles, mainly.
replies.liked_most: The nurse was wonderful with me.
replies.would_recommend: Yes, definitely. It made a real difference to how I manage things.
replies.staff_helpful: Yes, absolutely. Always available and very knowledgeable.

why: Every yes/no survey question carries elaboration in the same call. This is the
broadest test of the fix: none of the three yes/no slots (reviewed_resources,
would_recommend, staff_helpful) may trigger a retry or appear as declined.
participation_consent also carries a qualifier ('I've got a few minutes') to
confirm the gate slot survives the same pattern without breaking. The whole
survey must complete with all answers recorded correctly.

replies.reviewed_resources: No, I'm afraid I never got round to them.
no_review_reason: No time, really. Things have been hectic.
replies.improvement_feedback: More reminders to look at the resources would be useful.
replies.liked_most: The phone calls with the nurse were very helpful.

why: Trailing fragment ('I suppose it was mainly—') at no_review_reason, the choice
question on the no-resources branch, followed by a clear answer on re-ask.
This is the only scenario that exercises the trailing-fragment pattern on the
no_review_reason slot. It confirms the fix applies to a choice question on the
less-travelled branch: the fragment must not be guessed into an option, the
agent re-asks, and 'No time, really' maps to no_time on the second attempt.
no_review_reason must not appear as declined.

replies.reviewed_resources: Actually, something has just come up — I need to go. Could you call me back tomorrow afternoon, around two?
replies.reschedule_datetime: Tomorrow around two in the afternoon.

why: Reschedule requested at the very first survey question, with a datetime offered in
the same turn. Consent was given, the survey started, but before any answer is
recorded the member asks to be called back.
The turn must not be read as an answer to reviewed_resources. The call must end
immediately as reschedule_requested without recording any survey answer.

replies.reviewed_resources: I'm afraid I can't talk right now. Could we reschedule this call for another time?

why: Reschedule requested at the first survey question without a datetime in the same
turn. The agent must ask for a callback time, accept the answer, then close as
reschedule_requested.
Two-turn reschedule path mid-survey: the reschedule request is on the question
turn, and the datetime arrives on the next turn when asked.

replies.reviewed_resources: No. No. I'm telling you. I'm busy right now. Just reschedule this maybe tomorrow at two PM, I'll be free. Just call me then.

why: The exact transcript scenario: the member says 'No. No. I'm busy right now. Just
reschedule this maybe tomorrow at two PM' at the first survey question.
Two failures must not happen. First: the repeated 'No' must NOT be recorded as
the answer to reviewed_resources — it is emphatic frustration at being asked,
not a survey answer. Second: the call must not re-ask the question; the reschedule
request must be honoured immediately.
Expected outcome: reschedule_requested, no survey answers recorded at all.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I did look at some of the articles.
replies.improvement_feedback: I need to stop now, I'm sorry — something urgent has come up. Could you call me back next Monday morning?

why: Reschedule requested mid-survey after two questions are already answered. The
call must stop where it is — not continue, not discard what was already said.
reviewed_resources and resource_helpfulness must both survive in the outcome.
No question after the reschedule request may be asked. The disposition is
reschedule_requested, not partially_surveyed.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look at a few.
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular check-ins would be nice.
replies.would_recommend: Sorry, something urgent has just come up. Can you ring me back next Tuesday at eleven?

why: Reschedule near the end of the survey: four questions answered before the member
asks to stop. All four answers must survive in the outcome.
The 'sorry something urgent has come up' phrasing is the same as a CLOSING but
the reschedule request must take precedence over END_UNINTERESTED. The call
ends as reschedule_requested, not uninterested.

reviewed_resources: No. No. I'm not looking for that. I want to know more about my plan details.
Yes, I did look through some of the articles.

why: The user's exact reported scenario: 'No. No. I'm not looking for that, I want to
know details about my plan.' The repeated 'No' is an emphatic redirect — the
member is not answering reviewed_resources, they are stopping the caller to ask
about something else.
Three things must hold: the 'no' is not recorded as reviewed_resources (the
question is re-asked), the plan query is acknowledged as something this call
cannot action and reported as unsupported, and the 'yes' that arrives on the
second attempt lands correctly. reviewed_resources must not appear as declined.

reviewed_resources: Yes. Yes. I know. But I've been waiting three months for someone to call me back about a claim — nobody has rung.
Yes, I did go through some of the articles.
replies.liked_most: The information was easy to follow.

why: The 'yes yes' emphatic redirect: the member says 'Yes. Yes. I know. But I've been
waiting about a claim.' The repeated 'Yes' is impatience directed at the caller
('yes yes I heard you'), not an answer to whether they reviewed the resources.
The claim query is the member services entry that must reach the outcome.
reviewed_resources must be re-asked; on the second attempt 'yes' lands correctly.
reviewed_resources must not appear as declined.
Rising-tier member confirms staff_helpful is never asked and unsupported intent
reporting works on a different tier.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I had a look through a few.
resource_helpfulness: No. No. I don't want to rate that. I want to know why my portal account never worked — I could never log in.
replies.improvement_feedback: More regular phone calls would help.

why: Emphatic 'No. No.' redirect at a choice question rather than a yes/no question.
The member uses 'No. No. I don't want to rate that' to interrupt and raise a
portal access complaint — the 'no' is not a rating for resource_helpfulness.
The portal complaint is an unsupported service query and must reach the outcome.
resource_helpfulness must be re-asked; 'Somewhat helpful' on the second attempt
must land. resource_helpfulness must not appear as declined.
Confirms the emphatic-redirect detection is not limited to yes_no slots.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I looked at some of them.
replies.improvement_feedback: No. No. I've had enough of this survey now. Just end the call, please.

why: Emphatic 'No. No.' that ends the call rather than redirecting. 'No. No. I've had
enough of this survey now. Just end the call, please.' is an explicit refusal to
continue — not a reschedule request, not a service query.
This is the contrast case for emphatic_no_reschedule_with_datetime and the
redirect scenarios: the same emphatic 'No. No.' phrasing must produce
END_UNINTERESTED here because the content that follows ('end the call') is a
termination, not a question or a reschedule.
Answers from before the refusal must be kept. Nothing after it may be asked.

replies.participation_consent: No. No. Not right now — I'm really tied up. Can you reschedule for Friday at two PM?
replies.reviewed_resources: THIS MUST NEVER BE ASKED

why: Emphatic 'No. No.' reschedule request at the consent turn, with a datetime in the
same breath. The member is not simply declining consent — they are asking to be
called back at a specific time.
The key assertion: wants_reschedule (the spec slot the agent would normally ask
after a plain consent decline) must NEVER be asked. The reschedule request is
detected directly from the member's turn and the call closes as reschedule_
requested without going through the 'would you like to reschedule?' offer.
This confirms the fix applies at the consent gate, not just mid-survey, and that
a datetime offered in the reschedule turn reaches the outcome without a second ask.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, some of the articles.

why: The regression this scenario exists to catch: a bare 'Speaking.' with no
literal 'yes' anywhere in it, given as the very first reply to 'May I speak
to Margaret Ellison?'.
'Speaking' is the standard phone idiom for confirming identity when asked for
by name — there is no separate yes/no question being answered, the reply IS
the answer. A version of the extractor that requires a literal affirmative
word never records reached_policyholder from this turn, identity never
confirms, and the greeting is put again in slightly different words — which
reads, in a transcript, as the agent not having heard the member the first
time.
This is deliberately a single-string reply, not a list: if the gate does not
settle on the first turn, the script has nothing further to offer and the call
either loops until max_identity_asks is spent (surfacing as
representative_requested, not surveyed) or exhausts MAX_TURNS. Either failure
mode is caught by the disposition assertion alone.

replies.reviewed_resources: Yes, I looked at a few.
replies.liked_most: The nurse was very patient with me.

why: The other idiom nobody says 'yes' in: 'This is she', with no affirmative word
and no first-person pronoun either — the whole sentence identifies the speaker
only by the pronoun that stands in for the name just asked for.
Paired with bare_speaking_confirms_identity_first_try rather than merged with
it, because the two idioms fail independently: a fix that special-cases the
single word 'speaking' would still leave this one repeating the greeting.
